round2_dispositions.evidence: Live requests on create_app(): 405 carries 'allow: GET', 401 carries 'www-authenticate: Bearer realm="truelend"', 429 keeps 'retry-after: 42'; 404/422/500/200 envelopes and the X-Request-ID stamp unchanged.

Measured through the real class: 8-byte "1e100000" -> format() 4167.8 ms, fromWire 0.0 ms, toWire 2.5 ms; raw regex 4x per doubling of digits. Neither the constructor nor toWire() bounds the input. Only caller of format() is MoneyText, whose only callers are tests, so there is no untrusted path at HEAD. Tracked as CR-304.

findings.description: The `method` label is unbounded, so round-2's B-2 cardinality hole is only half-closed: f1367f5 bounded the route dimension but `method` still comes straight from scope["method"] into the keys of _request_counts and the new _duration_counts/_duration_totals. Measured against a real uvicorn server over raw sockets with http="h11" (uvicorn's own parser and its fallback when httptools is absent): 3000 distinct method tokens on one keep-alive connection in 0.7 s produced 2998 counter series + 2998 histogram series, a 3,553,759-byte /metrics body and ~2.5 MB permanently retained; /metrics is unauthenticated, so this amplifies too. Refutation attempted: with the declared uvicorn[standard]/httptools parser the same tokens get 400 before the app sees them, so the bound today rests entirely on an optional C extension's method allow-list that nothing in this repo documents, tests or pins - while middleware.py is deliberately written as a server-agnostic pure ASGI middleware and no Dockerfile/compose exists to fix the parser.
findings.fix: Add `_KNOWN_METHODS = frozenset({"GET","HEAD","POST","PUT","PATCH","DELETE","OPTIONS","TRACE"})` and a `method_label(scope)` returning the method when known and a single "<other>" bucket otherwise, mirroring `_UNMATCHED_ROUTE`; call it from `_stamping_send` and `_observe` in place of `str(scope.get("method", "-"))`. Add the h11 flood as the regression test.

findings.description: _escape_label escapes only backslash, double-quote and LF. CR, NUL, ESC and U+2028 pass through verbatim: with a CR in a label value, _histogram_lines() emits 14 lines containing a raw CR. E15-S4-AC2 requires 'no raw control character' when attacker-supplied control characters reach a metrics label, so the renderer fails the AC under the AC's own stated precondition. Not a BLOCK because the Prometheus exposition format only requires those three escapes (the docstring is accurate) and, once CR-301 is fixed, neither label source can carry a control character.
findings.fix: Extend _LABEL_ESCAPES to map \r to its escaped form and, cheaply, the rest of the C0 range, so the renderer satisfies AC2 independently of which labels happen to exist.

findings.description: The label-escaping fix has zero effective coverage. Reducing _escape_label to `return value` - deleting the whole B-1 remediation - leaves the suite green at 104 passed. Mutating route_label to the raw path instead fails four tests including both '...labels cannot be injected from a request path' (test_observability_contract.py:90 and test_health_probe.py:93), proving those two tests assert the cardinality bound, not the escaping. A future refactor can drop the escaping silently. The cumulative-bucket logic, by contrast, is covered: `running = count` fails test_histogram_buckets_are_cumulative_and_carry_count_and_sum.
findings.fix: Assert the escaping at the exposition boundary: after observe_duration with a quote- and backslash-bearing method label, require _histogram_lines() to contain the escaped form and no unescaped quote.

findings.description: Money.fromWire does not bound the input its docstring describes ('Parse the quoted 2dp wire string'): toQuantizedDecimal accepts anything decimal.js parses, so 8-byte "1e100000" reaches format() as 100,004 digits and the quadratic thousands-separator regex at line 78 costs 4167.8 ms (fromWire 0.0 ms, toWire 2.5 ms - the cost is isolated to the regex). WARN not BLOCK: format()'s only caller is MoneyText and its only callers are tests; the frontend at HEAD has no fetch layer and no input control, so there is no untrusted path and the impact is a client-side stall.
findings.fix: In toQuantizedDecimal, reject a string that does not match the wire form the backend declares (/^-?\d+\.\d{2}$/, backend/src/api/serializers.py:24) or cap the integer digit count, throwing InvalidMoneyAmountError. Choose the same tolerance as CR-306 so both sides of the wire agree.

findings.description: Both stated reasons for silencing uvicorn.access are untrue at HEAD. Claim (a) - 'request_id_var is already reset by the time it emits... it logs after the response completes, outside the middleware scope' - is false: uvicorn emits the access line inside its own send(), in the http.response.start branch (httptools_impl.py:484, h11_impl.py:481), and that send is the one CorrelationIdMiddleware wraps; replaying the ordering in-process shows request_id_var reads 'req-42' at that call site, not ''. It was true of the BaseHTTPMiddleware version CR-003 deleted. Claim (b) is overstated: RedactionFilter clears record.args only when a redaction actually fires (no registered values -> args preserved as ('a','b'); matching value -> ()).
findings.fix: Delete the two false sentences; keep the third (CorrelationIdMiddleware already emits an equivalent JSON line), which is the real and sufficient justification.

findings.description: The new JSON-schema hook works as claimed (model_json_schema renders; both a response model and a request-body model appear in components.schemas with the requestBody $ref intact - verified against a live /openapi.json), but the declared pattern is documentation only: no_info_plain_validator_function bypasses schema validation, so POST {"principal": "12.3"} returns 200 with "12.30" while the schema says 1dp is invalid. The docstring claims the pattern exists 'so a generated client cannot send 12.3 or a JSON number and still look contract-conformant'; only the JSON-number half is enforced (a float correctly 422s). backend/tests/architecture/test_no_float_money.py:342 asserts the documented pattern rejects '1234.5' while nothing checks the enforced behaviour.
findings.fix: Match a str input against _WIRE_PATTERN in _validate_money before constructing Money, or narrow the pattern and docstring to the tolerance actually implemented. Keep it consistent with CR-304.

findings.description: sanitise_context drops context values silently, with no marker and no log. Measured on live requests: {"note": "A"*300, "kept": "short"} -> {"kept":"short"}; {"ratio": 0.5, "flag": None} -> {}. Strings over _MAX_CONTEXT_VALUE_CHARS are discarded rather than truncated, and floats, None, lists and nested mappings vanish. context is the machine-readable half of the frozen envelope and src/types/errors.py:20 records that E4-S4-AC2 reads threshold_kind/configured_value out of it, so a caller cannot distinguish 'not set' from 'removed'. _scalar's docstring ('Anything structured is dropped') under-describes what actually goes.
findings.fix: Substitute a marker ("<omitted>") for the dropped key instead of deleting it, and truncate over-long strings to _MAX_CONTEXT_VALUE_CHARS rather than discarding them.

findings.description: `detail` bypasses the _CREDENTIAL_URI and length guards that context values get - it receives scrub_text() only, which is a no-op unless the exact value was registered. Measured: an AppError whose message interpolates a database URI carrying inline user:password credentials egresses those credentials verbatim in `detail`, while the identical string placed in `context` is dropped by _sanitise_value. Medium confidence because detail is developer-authored and handle_unexpected already pins a constant, but detail is the likeliest carrier of such a message, which is why the guard exists.
findings.fix: Run detail through the same _CREDENTIAL_URI and length check inside _envelope.

findings.description: _database_status swallows the probe's failure reason entirely: `except Exception: return "down"` with no log. The failure itself does reach the caller (database=down, status=degraded), so it is not a hidden error, but /health is the operator's only signal and a misconfigured probe is indistinguishable from a dead database with nothing in the logs.
findings.fix: Log at warning with exc_info=True before returning "down" - the traceback is already redaction-filtered by RedactionFilter.

findings.description: Avoidable `# type: ignore[arg-type]` in production code: begin_redaction_scope() -> object discards the Token type ContextVar.set returns, forcing the ignore on the reset. CLAUDE.md requires static typing everywhere. Verified the fix is clean - typing both as contextvars.Token[set[str] | None] and deleting the ignore gives `mypy src/` Success (12 files) and 104 passed (applied, verified, reverted).
findings.fix: Import Token from contextvars; type begin_redaction_scope's return and end_redaction_scope's parameter as Token[set[str] | None]; delete the type: ignore.

findings.description: Round-2's finding is unfixed: both AC2 'every logger has the filter' tests (lines 43-64 and 190-220) build their logger list from logging.root.manager.loggerDict - the same collection _install_redaction_filter_everywhere (logging.py:241-251) just iterated - so a logger created after configure_logging is invisible to the assertion by construction. The 'unregistered-probe-logger' control proves the predicate works, not that the enumeration is complete. The real guarantee comes from the RedactionFilter on the root handler (logging.py:199), covered behaviourally by test_sensitive_application_values_never_appear_in_any_log_line.
findings.fix: Add one case that creates a logger after configure_logging, gives it its own handler with propagate=False, and asserts a registered value is still redacted - the case the enumeration cannot see.

findings.description: `assert p95_bound == "+Inf" or float(p95_bound) <= 0.5` accepts the unbounded bucket, so the assertion passes when p95 exceeds every declared bound - the exact opposite of the comment above it ('A no-I/O health probe must land far under the 500 ms budget'). The test proves p95 is computable (E15-S4-AC1's main claim) but asserts nothing about its value.

The process-global metric state (_request_counts, _duration_counts, _duration_totals) has no enforced test isolation - it holds today only because every count-asserting test remembers reset_request_counters() first (verified across three orderings: file alone 6 passed, file last after the whole suite 104 passed, reordered 8 passed). One future test that forgets it silently inherits another test's counts. reset_request_counters() is also production API whose docstring says it exists 'For tests'.
findings.fix: Add an autouse fixture in backend/tests/conftest.py calling reset_request_counters(), making isolation structural rather than conventional.

findings.description: The counter is incremented before `await send(message)`, so a response that fails mid-send is still recorded as served: with a send that raises at http.response.start, request_counter_snapshot() shows {('GET','/health',200): 1}. Minor over-count of successes in the SLO signal.
findings.fix: Increment after the await, or accept the over-count and note it.

findings.description: latency_bucket_bounds() is a single-use getter returning a module constant that routes.py could import directly - a borderline shallow wrapper under code-gen principle 8, kept only to preserve the leading-underscore convention.
findings.fix: Leave as is, or export _LATENCY_BUCKETS as LATENCY_BUCKETS and drop the getter.

findings.description: _observe is called on both the success and exception branches rather than once in a finally - a duplicated call site; and if _observe itself raised inside the try, the except would record a second observation.
findings.fix: Move the single _observe call into a finally block, keeping the exception logging in except.

findings.description: Refuted, recorded for coverage. zip(..., strict=True) is safe: both lengths derive from the module-level _LATENCY_BUCKETS tuple and observe_duration sizes the list from the same constant. The linear bucket scan (middleware.py:80-83) is not a perf concern - 11 comparisons per request, below measurement noise. Bucket `le` semantics verified correct (0.005 -> bucket 0, 0.0050001 -> bucket 1, 0.5 -> bucket 6, 11.0 and NaN -> +Inf). The exception path was verified to record both a duration and a counter with X-Request-ID present on the 500.

A 7-line paragraph justifies deliberately not unwinding two contextvars on the failure path. The decision is sound and the reason is real, but this is the shape the code-gen paragraph rule warns about.
findings.fix: Compress to one line plus the story/finding reference (CR-003, E15-S1-AC4).
